gaps.gap: BAML v1 (the current, public-beta language) was not read by any lane. D, R and P all fell back to v0/legacy docs. new.boundaryml.com shows v1 `test`/`testset` syntax, and https://boundaryml.com/agent/guide (found by search, never fetched) may be its agent guide.
gaps.why_it_matters: Most cards on prompt tests, asserts, retry and SAP (landing areas a and b) describe a version BoundaryML now calls legacy. Any idea taken from v0 test blocks may not match how the vendor now frames tests for agents and CI.
gaps.how_to_close: Fetch boundaryml.com/agent/guide and the v1 docs it links from new.boundaryml.com. Diff the v1 test, testset, assert and parse semantics against cards D-02/D-03/D-07/R-06.

gaps.gap: Nobody read the SAP parser source in BoundaryML/baml (the Rust jsonish/coercion code under the engine workspace). Its behaviour comes only from vendor prose and one issue (#4590).
gaps.why_it_matters: Landing area (a) depends on whether lenient parsing silently drops or coerces data. Our Workflow contracts depend on strict schema validation with retry. Whether SAP's coercion matches 'honest-empty, never fabricate' is a code question, not a docs question.
gaps.how_to_close: Use the api.github.com contents/search endpoint to find the jsonish/coercer crate on canary. Read its array and enum coercion paths and the tests that assert lossy behaviour.

gaps.gap: No lane covered general prompt-regression tooling outside BAML, such as promptfoo, Inspect AI or OpenAI Evals. Lane P covered only Pydantic evals and DSPy.
gaps.why_it_matters: Landing area (b), 'we have NO tests of briefs', is the strongest idea candidate. BAML's test blocks can't run inside plain-JS Workflow scripts, so the closest usable models are tools that are independent of language and provider.
gaps.how_to_close: A short prior-art pass reading the promptfoo assertion/test-case docs and Inspect AI's dataset/scorer docs, compared with the BAML test cards.

gaps.gap: Nobody read the docs for the harness's own structured-output layer: Claude Code Workflow/Agent SDK structured output and the StructuredOutput tool's retry-on-mismatch behaviour. Only Anthropic API structured-output pages were read (I-12..I-14).
gaps.why_it_matters: Each card that maps to area (a) compares BAML with our mechanism. Without the SDK-level semantics (retry count, what happens on repeated failure, enum or required strictness), 'BAML does X better' claims about area (a) can't be checked.
gaps.how_to_close: Fetch the Claude Code / Agent SDK structured-outputs docs page and record its retry and failure contract next to cards D-08, D-11 and I-12.

coverage_verdict: Broad v0 and vendor coverage in all six lanes; the gaps that could change the review are v1 docs, the SAP source code, and prompt-test prior art outside BAML.
